findings.claim: The ground the row gives for declining its strongest rival is an un-digited book-wide typicality claim, coupled with a tier-3 parashah mark carried as a co-equal reason.
findings.grounds: The rejected-alternative field states that the frame at oshb:Isa.42.5, כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte), is 'the book's ordinary marker for a new unit' with no sweep digit anywhere in the row, and adds 'a parashah PE mark closes the preceding span immediately before it, at oshb:Isa.42.4' as a second coordinate because-clause. Re-swept with the object named: the koh-amar formula stands in 48 verses book-wide and in exactly 4 verses within chs 41-43 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16), none in ch 41 -- the digit the book-order neighbor row carries for the identical warrant and this row does not. MT 42:4 is PE in the inventory (type correct, single-witness disclosed), but prophets-parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver. The onset itself is sound: the koh-amar frame stands in the cited verse's own bytes.
findings.proposed_change: In strongest_rejected_alternative, attach the digit-bearing sweep already available for this object (sweep: 4 verses, the koh-amar formula within chs 41-43, all four divine-owned) to the typicality clause, and recast the PE clause at oshb:Isa.42.4 as corroboration rather than a coordinate because-ground.

findings.claim: A sweep digit is shipped for a count object this row's prose never argues, and the digit names no domain -- as written it is false at book scope.
findings.grounds: device_notes carries '(sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42; 2 verses, the kavod noun)'. The tehillah digit verifies exactly: the tehillah noun stands in 3 verses of ch 42 (MT 42:8, 42:10, 42:12). The kavod half names no domain, and this row makes no kavod claim at all -- no glory-noun run, ref, or thread appears anywhere in its prose. Re-swept with the object named: the kavod noun stands in 35 verses book-wide and in 2 verses of ch 42 (MT 42:8, 42:12), so '2 verses, the kavod noun' is true only under a domain the citation does not state. The book-order neighbor row is where the glory-noun thread is actually argued.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the kavod half of the parenthetical from this row; or, if the glory-noun thread is to be argued here, add the claim it backs and state its domain as the tehillah half already does ('2 verses, the kavod noun in ch 42').

findings.claim: The row's cross-seam new-things/new-song disclosure declares tier NONE for the attested tokens; re-collation returns skeleton tier in one direction.
findings.grounds: device_notes says the new-things and new-song forms share 'the root at stem level, the attested tokens themselves returning tier NONE'. Re-collated with the staged collator: the attested new-song token חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) returns SKELETON tier against oshb:Isa.42.9; only the reverse direction, וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ (oshb:Isa.42.9, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.42.10, returns none. The claim is stated symmetrically and is false as written. Impact is bounded: this row's own dismissal already runs at skeleton tier ('a skeleton-tier cohesion driver is disclosed texture'), so the cut survives the correction -- the tier label does not.
findings.proposed_change: Restate as skeleton tier with the direction named (the new-song token re-collates against oshb:Isa.42.9 at skeleton tier; the reverse returns none), leaving the existing skeleton-tier dismissal reasoning to carry the cut unchanged.

findings.claim: Review-process framing in row prose: a thread is called 'undisclosed' in the same sentence that discloses it.
findings.grounds: device_notes opens 'This unit's own close seam carries an undisclosed thread:' and then discloses that thread in full. 'Undisclosed' describes the review record, not the text, and is administrative register inside a shipped row field.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'carries an undisclosed thread' with a textual formulation such as 'carries a thread that crosses it'.

findings.claim: Two WEB runs in the load-bearing boundary field are carried without curly delimiters, leaving the quoted extent undetermined and outside the verbatim checker's reach.
findings.grounds: The web:Isa.42.5 run carries no curly quotation marks at all, and the web:Isa.42.9 run ends on a closing curly mark that is WEB's own text rather than a delimiter; the field's curly counts are 0 open / 1 close. Both runs were re-checked against the WEB witness and are verbatim, so this is a delimiting shortfall only. The book-order neighbor rows in the same chapter delimit their WEB runs on both sides.
findings.proposed_change: Wrap both WEB runs in curly double quotes, keeping WEB's own internal quotation marks intact.

findings.claim: The row declares tier NONE for the attested new-things/new-song tokens crossing its own opening seam; re-collation returns skeleton tier in one direction.
findings.grounds: device_notes says the new-song phrase takes up the new-things phrase 'at stem level, the attested tokens themselves returning tier NONE'. Re-collated: חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, tier: byte) returns SKELETON against oshb:Isa.42.9; וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ (oshb:Isa.42.9, tier: byte) returns none against oshb:Isa.42.10. The summary sentence 'None of the three rises above a skeleton- or stem-level thread' still holds after the correction, so the row's high confidence is not disturbed; the tier label on this one pair is.
findings.proposed_change: Name the tier as skeleton with the direction disclosed, leaving the 'none of the three rises above a skeleton- or stem-level thread' summary and the confidence unchanged.

findings.claim: A sweep digit names its count object but no domain, and is false at book scope.
findings.grounds: device_notes carries '(sweep: 2 verses, the kavod noun)'. Re-swept: the kavod noun stands in 35 verses book-wide and in 2 verses of ch 42 (MT 42:8, 42:12). The digit is right only under a domain the citation does not state, while the tehillah digit in the same device_notes does state its domain ('3 verses, the tehillah noun in ch 42' -- verified exact at MT 42:8, 42:10, 42:12).
findings.proposed_change: State the domain: '(sweep: 2 verses, the kavod noun in ch 42)'.

findings.claim: Campaign-workflow vocabulary in row prose.
findings.grounds: device_notes states 'no deviation from the closed unit_type vocabulary is registered here' -- a statement about the campaign's controlled vocabulary and its registration process, not about the text.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the clause; the unit_type field already carries the vocabulary commitment.

findings.claim: The closing WEB run in the boundary field is carried without curly delimiters.
findings.grounds: The web:Isa.42.13 run ('Yahweh will go out like a mighty man ... He will triumph over his enemies.') carries no curly quotation marks; the field's one curly pair belongs to the web:Isa.42.10 run. The web:Isa.42.13 wording was re-checked against the WEB witness and is verbatim.
findings.proposed_change: Wrap the web:Isa.42.13 run in curly double quotes.

findings.claim: A tier-3 parashah mark is the leading because-ground for refusing the row's strongest rival.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative: folding MT 42:17 forward 'was proposed but not adopted, because the parashah SAMEKH mark closes at oshb:Isa.42.17 rather than before it, and the idol-trusters named there are third-person objects ... not the deaf-and-blind addressees the imperative of oshb:Isa.42.18 opens with.' The mark is the first of two coordinate causal grounds, not a corroborator. Inventory check: MT 42:17 is SAMEKH (type correct, single-witness disclosed), but prophets-parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver. The second ground -- the participant contrast between the third-person idol-trusters of MT 42:17 and the addressees of the imperative at MT 42:18 -- is a genuine text ground and independently carries the refusal, so the seam holds.
findings.proposed_change: Lead the refusal with the participant/addressee ground standing in the bytes of MT 42:17 against MT 42:18, and demote the SAMEKH clause to explicit corroboration.

findings.claim: The row's only cross-seam cohesion disclosure ships with no pointed splice and no tier label, on the translation witness.
findings.grounds: The whole of device_notes reads: 'The blind-guiding promise of web:Isa.42.16 anticipates the blind-servant address of web:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19 in the following span; this row discloses the shared imagery as a cross-seam echo without merging the two spans.' The device straddles this row's own close seam and is boundary-relevant, yet no Hebrew is spliced and no tier is named, against the engagement class and the tier-label-every-recurrence standard. Re-collated, the device is real and gradable: עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, tier: byte) returns ACCENT_STRIPPED tier against oshb:Isa.42.18, where וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.18, tier: byte) stands. The book-order neighbor row discloses the same device with both splices and the accent_stripped tier named, so this row is the outlier.
findings.proposed_change: Splice the blindness lexeme at oshb:Isa.42.16 and oshb:Isa.42.18 and name the accent_stripped tier, matching the disclosure the neighbor row already carries for the same device.

findings.claim: The opening WEB run is never closed, leaving its extent undetermined.
findings.grounds: The web:Isa.42.14 run opens on WEB's own curly quotation mark and runs into ', pointed' with no closing delimiter; the field's curly counts are 1 open / 0 close. The wording was re-checked against the WEB witness and is verbatim.
findings.proposed_change: Close the WEB run with a curly quotation mark before the pointed splice.

findings.claim: The row's own close seam is supported by nothing but a tier-3 parashah mark; no tier-1 signal is named for it anywhere in the boundary field.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale closes with only: 'It closes at web:Isa.42.25. A parashah PE mark (single-witness) closes at oshb:Isa.42.25, corroborating the break.' The mark is said to corroborate a break that no tier-1 signal in the row establishes, and prophets-parashah is never a boundary driver. Inventory check: MT 42:25 is PE (type correct). The signal that actually carries this seam is the divine-speech frame opening the next unit, וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) -- one of only 4 koh-amar verses in chs 41-43 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16; 48 book-wide) -- which appears in this row only inside a device_notes name-pair thread and is never named as the close warrant. The seam location is sound; the warrant as shipped is not.
findings.proposed_change: Name the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.1 in the boundary field as the tier-1 signal carrying the close, with its pointed splice and tier, and keep the PE mark at oshb:Isa.42.25 as corroboration.

findings.claim: The fire-verb device straddling the row's own close seam is declared tier NONE; re-collation returns skeleton tier in one direction.
findings.grounds: device_notes: וַתִּבְעַר (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) 'is answered by' the clause at oshb:Isa.43.2, 'the two sharing only the fire-verb stem, the attested tokens returning tier NONE'. Re-collated: the attested token תִבְעַר (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte) returns SKELETON tier against oshb:Isa.42.25; only the reverse direction returns none. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless honestly disclosed, and understating the tier from skeleton to none understates that counter-pressure. The seam still holds on the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.1.
findings.proposed_change: Restate the pair at skeleton tier with the direction named.

findings.claim: The sole refusal ground for the row's strongest rival is an original-language form claim carried unspliced on the translation witness, and the unit's extent is described by a tier-4 chapter division.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative refuses an internal split because 'no fresh imperative, addressee, or divine-speech-frame formula opens web:Isa.42.21', then bounds the unit as running 'through to the chapter's close'. The form claim is boundary-relevant original-language content but ships with no pointed splice and keyed to the WEB witness; the extent clause rests on a chapter division, which is tier-4 metadata and never boundary evidence. Checked against the bytes, the form claim is true: MT 42:21 reads יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר (oshb:Isa.42.21, tier: byte) -- no speech frame, no imperative -- so the rival is rightly refused, on a ground the row does not evidence to standard.
findings.proposed_change: Splice MT 42:21 and cite it as oshb:Isa.42.21 for the absence-of-frame ground, and replace 'through to the chapter's close' with the verse-anchored extent (through web:Isa.42.25).

findings.claim: Writer-part workflow vocabulary in row prose.
findings.grounds: device_notes states 'The close seam is a cross-part seam and carries two further devices'. 'Cross-part' names the campaign's writer-part slicing, not a property of the text, and is administrative register in a shipped field.
findings.proposed_change: Delete 'is a cross-part seam and'; the devices disclosed after it stand on their own.

findings.claim: The row enumerates all four collation tiers as failing for the fire-catchword pair on its own opening seam; re-collation returns skeleton tier in one direction.
findings.grounds: device_notes: the pair is said to share 'only the burn/kindle root, with the attested tokens matching at none of the byte, nfd, accent-stripped, or skeleton tiers (tier NONE)'. Re-collated: תִבְעַר (oshb:Isa.43.2, tier: byte) returns SKELETON tier against oshb:Isa.42.25, where וַתִּבְעַר (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) stands; only the reverse direction returns none. The claim is stated symmetrically and names skeleton explicitly among the tiers that fail, so it is false as written. It is also the disclosure on which the row rests its judgement that the cross-seam devices 'argue continuity across the seam without disturbing the cut', so the corrected tier changes the disclosed weight of a device on the row's own seam. The cut itself is unaffected: the onset וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) is a tier-1 divine-speech frame.
findings.proposed_change: Restate as skeleton tier in the oshb:Isa.43.2 to oshb:Isa.42.25 direction and none in the reverse, keeping the continuity-without-disturbance judgement, which survives at skeleton tier.

findings.claim: The shared 43:7|43:8 seam is argued incompatibly by this row and its book-order neighbor: this row's refusal ground places 43:8's affinity backward, away from the very unit the neighbor row opens at 43:8.
findings.grounds: This row refuses its rival because עִוֵּ֖ר stands at oshb:Isa.43.8 as 'a distinct summons of the blind people' whose byte-tier tie runs to oshb:Isa.42.19 -- 'reaching back rather than forward into the nations' gathering'. The neighbor row makes oshb:Isa.43.8 the onset verse of the gathering-trial unit and grounds that onset on a participant shift it discloses it cannot fix at form level. Both rows place the seam at the same point, so no span is in dispute; the stated affinity of the opening verse is. The byte tie itself verifies: עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte) returns BYTE tier against oshb:Isa.42.19.
findings.proposed_change: Reconcile the two rows' stated grounds for the 43:7|43:8 seam so the blind-word tie is described the same way on both sides -- a backward lexical echo carried by a verse that nonetheless opens the following unit -- without moving the seam.

findings.claim: Writer-part workflow vocabulary in two fields.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative carries 'the same pointed word recurring at byte tier one part earlier'; device_notes carries 'straddles the row's own opening seam at the part boundary'. Both name the campaign's writer-part slicing rather than any property of the text.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'one part earlier' with the verse-anchored locator (at oshb:Isa.42.19) and drop 'at the part boundary'.

findings.claim: Three curly-quoted WEB English runs are bound to oshb: (MT) refs in the load-bearing boundary field.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale cites the run 'Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.' at (oshb:Isa.43.8), the run 'Let all the nations be gathered together...Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified' at (oshb:Isa.43.9), and the run 'You are my witnesses, says Yahweh' at (oshb:Isa.43.10). Each wording was re-checked and is verbatim WEB at the corresponding web: ref, and none of it is MT text; the oshb: prefix names the Hebrew witness for translation runs. The mandatory pairing of curly quotes with an in-field web: ref is therefore not met at these three citations. The oshb:Isa.43.10 run additionally re-renders WEB's own curly inner quotation marks as straight ones, so it is not character-verbatim as shipped.
findings.proposed_change: Re-key the three English runs to web:Isa.43.8, web:Isa.43.9 and web:Isa.43.10, and restore WEB's curly inner quotation marks in the web:Isa.43.10 run.

findings.claim: The strongest-rejected-alternative field states the rival and records no ground for rejecting it.
findings.grounds: The field reads in full: 'A rival reading folds the row into the fear-not oracle preceding it as one extended first-person address, treating the witness-summons of Isa.43.9 as a turn rather than a fresh trial frame.' No refusal clause follows. The only onset ground the row offers anywhere is the participant shift at oshb:Isa.43.8, עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, tier: byte), which the row itself discloses it cannot fix at form level ('no per-token parsing layer is staged to fix an imperative or vocative shape at this verse'), so the record does not show the rejection was earned. The neighbor rows on both sides carry explicit refusal clauses for their own rivals.
findings.proposed_change: Add the refusal ground to the field -- the participant change at oshb:Isa.43.8 against the addressed second person running through oshb:Isa.43.1-43.7 -- keeping the field within its one-sentence limit.

findings.claim: Both parashah citations are keyed to the WEB witness, and the in-span mark is never disclosed in prose.
findings.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.43.10 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.43.13 (setumah, single-witness)'. Checked against the inventory, both marks exist and both are SAMEKH at the MT keys, and ch 43 is identity-numbered so no arithmetic error follows; but the parashah layer is MT-keyed and these citations carry the WEB prefix. The MT 43:10 mark also sits inside this row's span and is never disclosed in any prose field.
findings.proposed_change: Re-key both mark citations to oshb:Isa.43.10 and oshb:Isa.43.13, and disclose the in-span MT 43:10 mark in prose with its single-witness label.

findings.claim: Campaign and tooling vocabulary in row prose.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale carries 'no per-token parsing layer is staged to fix an imperative or vocative shape at this verse' and 'the byte census leaves that servant figure unnamed here'; device_notes carries 'sits among the servant-figure sites the campaign holds unnamed'. All three name the staging infrastructure or the campaign itself rather than the text.
findings.proposed_change: Recast as textual statements (the verse's own bytes do not fix the form; the verse does not name the servant), removing the staging and campaign references.

findings.claim: The row's only close warrant is an original-language formula claim asserted with no pointed splice and keyed to the translation witness.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale closes: the unit 'closes two verses later on ... (web:Isa.43.15), just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16.' Nothing else supports the close. The frame is boundary-relevant original-language content and ships unspliced under a web: ref, against the mandatory engagement class. Checked against the bytes the claim is true: MT 43:16 opens כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte), one of only 4 koh-amar verses in chs 41-43 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16). The seam is sound; the warrant as shipped is not evidenced to standard.
findings.proposed_change: Splice the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.16 with its tier named as the close warrant, alongside the existing web: reference.

findings.claim: The strongest-rejected-alternative field records only the rival's own supporting reasons and no ground for rejecting it, on a rival that would merge this span away.
findings.grounds: The field reads: 'A rival reading keeps this two-verse Redeemer announcement joined to the new-thing oracle that follows as one Babylon-and-exodus complex, since both open on a Yahweh...says pattern and share the redemption theme.' The since-clause argues for the rival; no counter is recorded. Adopting the rival would merge Isa.43.14-Isa.43.15 into the following unit, so the gap is span-relevant. The ground that defeats it exists in the bytes and is not stated in the field: MT 43:16 opens its own frame, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte), and MT 43:14 opens another, so two frames stand where the rival sees one complex.
findings.proposed_change: Record the refusal in the field: two distinct koh-amar frames stand at oshb:Isa.43.14 and oshb:Isa.43.16, which is what separates the two units rather than joining them.

findings.claim: Both parashah citations are keyed to the WEB witness.
findings.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.43.13 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.43.15 (setumah, single-witness)'. Checked against the inventory, both marks exist and both are SAMEKH at the MT keys, and ch 43 is identity-numbered so no arithmetic error follows; the parashah layer is MT-keyed and these citations carry the WEB prefix.
findings.proposed_change: Re-key both mark citations to oshb:Isa.43.13 and oshb:Isa.43.15.

findings.claim: A closure key is registered where no closure device stands in the row's own closing verse.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries 'oracle_frame.short_oracle_closure'. The row's closing verse reads אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה קְדֽוֹשְׁכֶ֑ם בּוֹרֵ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מַלְכְּכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.43.15, tier: byte) -- a divine self-predication with the Holy One, Creator and King titles, territory the row's 'divine_title.redeemer_holy_one' entry already covers. No closure device stands there; the key encodes the span's brevity, which is a property of the row rather than a substrate signal.
findings.proposed_change: Drop 'oracle_frame.short_oracle_closure', or replace it with a key naming the device that actually stands in oshb:Isa.43.15 (the divine self-predication).

findings.claim: Both parashah citations are keyed to the WEB witness.
findings.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.43.15 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.43.21 (setumah, single-witness)'. Checked against the inventory, both marks exist and both are SAMEKH at the MT keys, and ch 43 is identity-numbered so no arithmetic error follows; the parashah layer is MT-keyed and these citations carry the WEB prefix.
findings.proposed_change: Re-key both mark citations to oshb:Isa.43.15 and oshb:Isa.43.21.

findings.claim: An oss key labels the span's participle chain as a creator chain; no creation verb stands in either verse.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries 'divine_title.creator_participle_chain'. The chain the row itself splices is הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte) and הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב וָס֖וּס (oshb:Isa.43.17, tier: byte) -- a way-giving epithet and an army-leading epithet. Neither verse carries a creation verb; the creation verbs in this run of oracles stand at oshb:Isa.43.1, oshb:Isa.43.7 and oshb:Isa.43.15, all outside this span. The key names a title class the span's own bytes do not support.
findings.proposed_change: Rename the key to the epithet class the bytes support (a participle-chain divine title of way-making and deliverance), leaving the other two entries unchanged.

findings.claim: The strongest-rejected-alternative field records only the rival's supporting reason; the refusal ground is present but placed in device_notes.
findings.grounds: The field states the internal-split rival 'since the prohibitive-and-presentative address is a distinct move from the third-person description that opens the row', with no counter. The counter is carried in device_notes instead ('neither carries its own koh-amar or addressee-shift marker'). Checked against the bytes the counter holds: אַֽל תִּזְכְּר֖וּ (oshb:Isa.43.18, tier: byte) and הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה (oshb:Isa.43.19, tier: byte) open no frame, and the messenger formula opened at oshb:Isa.43.16 is not closed on the WEB page until the 'says:' ending web:Isa.43.17, so the participles and the new-thing speech stand inside one frame. The grouping is sound; the field that rejects the rival does not carry the reason.
findings.proposed_change: Move the refusal ground into strongest_rejected_alternative, within the field's one-sentence limit.
